items.label: Past Tense
items.text: "She opened the door. The hallway stretched ahead of her." Events have already happened. Past tense lets you control pacing through temporal compression: "The next three hours were quiet" is easy. Action sequences stay punchy. Reflection feels organic.

items.label: Present Tense
items.text: "She opens the door. The hallway stretches ahead of her." Events happen NOW. Present tense creates immediacy and urgency. the character doesn't know what happens next because it hasn't happened yet. The trade-off is pacing: you can't easily skip time, and every moment carries equal weight. Works best for action-heavy, tension-heavy, or stream-of-consciousness scenes. Harder to sustain over long sessions but electric when it lands.

items.label: Future Tense
items.text: "She will open the door. The hallway will stretch ahead of her." Events haven't happened yet. Prophetic, dreamlike, fatalistic. This is weird and that's the point. Future tense implies inevitability: things WILL happen, and neither character nor reader can stop them. Use sparingly. Works for prophecy, fate-driven narratives, or deliberately unsettling prose. Not recommended for general RP unless you're doing something very specific.
